h1: Video production, animation and AI video for Islamabad organisations
intro: 22 Signals handles video production for Islamabad organisations: explainer animations for programmes and public messaging, brand films, reels for social, 2D and 3D animation, and AI video that is clearly labelled and checked by a person. We script in English and Urdu, add subtitles, and can broadcast live events when the date cannot move.

sections.h: What Islamabad organisations need video for
p: Video in the capital does a wider range of jobs than in a city built on retail. A development programme needs a three-minute animation that explains a new service to families who may not read well. A telecom needs a launch film and twenty short cuts for social. A university needs an admissions reel and a convocation livestream. A software exporter needs a product demo its US sales team can send. A think tank needs its report turned into something people will watch on a phone.

Each job needs a different format, tone and length. Before any video production, Islamabad clients get the same three questions from us: who will watch, where, and in what language? Only then do we pick the camera, the animation style or the AI tool.

list: Short-form video and reels for Instagram, TikTok, YouTube Shorts and LinkedIn
2D and 3D animation, including product and technical animation
AI video: AI presenters, ad variations and generated scenes, labelled and reviewed
Managed editing teams for organisations with a steady flow of footage
Live broadcast of conferences, launches and events

sections.h: Explainers for programmes and public messaging
p: Animation suits public information work. It avoids identifying real beneficiaries, it can show processes that are hard to film, and it can be revoiced for other languages without reshooting. We write the script with your programme team, test it for plain language, and record Urdu and English voiceovers, with subtitles in regional languages such as Pashto or Punjabi where your audience needs them.
For donor-funded work we follow the visibility and branding rules in your grant agreement, and keep a record of approvals for each version.

list: NGOs and international organisations: awareness explainers, case story films with consent recorded, and donor report videos
Telecoms and their partners: product launches, tariff explainers and social cut-downs
Universities and schools: admissions films, campus tours, lecture capture and convocation streams
Software exporters and startups: product demos, pitch videos for investor days and recruitment films
Hospitals and clinics: patient information animations and doctor introduction videos
Real estate developers: project films and construction progress updates, often combined with 3D animation

p: AI video can produce ad variations, translated presenter clips and backgrounds quickly. In Islamabad, where public trust and misinformation are live issues, it also needs care. We label AI-generated content clearly, never clone a real person's face or voice without written consent, and have a person review every frame before anything is published.
For public-facing organisations we usually keep AI to supporting roles, such as backgrounds, variations and drafts, and use real presenters for anything that speaks for you.

Some locations in the capital, including the Red Zone and the Diplomatic Enclave, need permissions before any camera comes out, and many offices and hospitals have their own rules. When your project needs live-action footage, we plan the shoot with your team: locations, permissions, consent forms, schedule and shot list. A crew is arranged when the project needs it, and much of the post-production, animation and AI work happens remotely from London.

Weather and light shape the schedule too. Outdoor shoots in Islamabad are planned around the monsoon months, with a spare day held for rain, and the Margalla Hills give a backdrop worth timing for the late afternoon light.

sections.h: Proof: live events run to the minute
p: We have run and broadcast more than 20 large-scale live events. That experience shapes how we approach a conference stream, a launch event or a convocation in Islamabad: rehearsal, backup connections, a running order agreed in writing, and someone accountable for every minute on air.

list: Talk: the audience, the message, the platforms and the deadline
Plan: script, storyboard or style frames, schedule and approvals, all in writing
Build: shooting, animation or AI work, editing, sound and subtitles, reviewed with time-stamped comments
Grow: cut-downs for each platform, performance review and the next round of content, owned by your Signal Lead

sections.h: Working with us from Islamabad, and cost factors
p: We work with Islamabad organisations remotely from our head office in London. Drafts are reviewed online with comments pinned to the exact frame, and review calls sit in the Islamabad afternoon: 10:30 London is 15:30 PKT in winter, 14:30 PKT in summer. Final files are delivered in every format you need.

We do not publish prices for video production. Islamabad projects are costed on length, format (live action, animation, AI or a mix), number of languages and versions, filming days and permissions, music and voiceover licensing, and turnaround time.

A search for video production Islamabad usually starts with one film, and the film is rarely the only thing needed. The team making your video also runs ads, SEO, websites and 3D work, so a film can launch with its landing page, ad cut-downs and search pages ready on the same day. Related: 3D rendering, paid media in Islamabad, and our global video and motion service.

faqs.q: Do you have a film crew in Islamabad?
faqs.a: No. We do not have an office or a standing crew in Islamabad. When live-action filming is needed, we plan it with you and arrange a crew when the project needs it. Many projects need no filming at all: animation, motion graphics, AI video and editing of your existing footage are all handled remotely.

faqs.q: Can you produce videos in Urdu?
faqs.a: Yes. We write scripts in Urdu and English, record voiceovers with native speakers, and design on-screen text in proper Urdu typography. We can also produce subtitles in Urdu, English and other languages your audience needs. Each language version is checked by a person who reads it fluently.

faqs.q: How do you handle consent in case story films?
faqs.a: We use written consent forms that explain where the video will appear and for how long, in a language the person understands. For vulnerable people we follow your organisation's safeguarding policy and often recommend animation or voice-only formats instead. Consent records are stored with the project files.

faqs.q: Is AI video appropriate for a public organisation?
faqs.a: It can be, used carefully. AI works well for backgrounds, quick variations and draft versions. We label AI content clearly and avoid AI presenters for official statements or anything that could be mistaken for a real person speaking for you. Every AI output is reviewed by a person before publication.

faqs.q: Can you livestream our conference or convocation?
faqs.a: Yes. We plan the stream with your venue and team, run rehearsals, set up backup connections and manage the broadcast on YouTube, Facebook or your own platform. We have broadcast more than 20 large-scale live events, so the running order and the backup plan are agreed in writing well before the day.

faqs.q: How long does an explainer animation take?
faqs.a: It depends on length, style and how many people approve the script. We agree a schedule at the start, from script to final delivery, and put it in writing. The step that most often slows things down is script approval, so we keep the number of review rounds clear from day one.
